definitions.gloss: extra edition; special edition (of a newspaper)
definitions.explanation: A special newspaper edition published outside the regular schedule to report breaking news of major importance. Traditionally distributed free on the street.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}で{号外|ごうがい}を{配|くば}っていた。
examples.english: They were handing out extra editions in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {戦争|せんそう}{終結|しゅうけつ}のニュースが{号外|ごうがい}で{伝|つた}えられ、{人々|ひとびと}は{歓声|かんせい}を{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: The news of the war's end was announced in an extra edition, and people cheered.

notes:
Composed of {号|ごう} (number, issue) and {外|がい} (outside) — literally an issue 'outside' the regular numbering. A {号外|ごうがい} is published only for truly major events: elections, natural disasters, historic achievements, or declarations of war/peace.

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, {号外|ごうがい} are traditionally single-sheet papers distributed by hand near train stations. Even in the digital age, major newspapers still print physical {号外|ごうがい} for landmark events, and crowds gather to receive them as keepsakes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {号外|ごうがい}が{出|で}る — an extra edition comes out
- {号外|ごうがい}を{配|くば}る — to distribute extra editions
- {号外|ごうがい}を{出|だ}す — to publish an extra edition

RELATED WORDS:
- {夕刊|ゆうかん} — evening edition (of a newspaper)
- {朝刊|ちょうかん} — morning edition (of a newspaper)
- {臨時|りんじ}ニュース — breaking news bulletin (broadcast equivalent)
